prompt:
Some people argue that the main purpose of a university education should be to prepare students for employment, rather than to give them knowledge for its own sake.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: State your position clearly in the introduction and keep it consistent to the end
Address the idea that universities should mainly prepare students for jobs
Address the alternative: knowledge for its own sake
Support each main idea with explanation and a specific example
Write a conclusion that restates your position (no new ideas)

for: Students pay high fees and take on debt, so they reasonably expect better job prospects
Economies need graduates with practical, up-to-date skills (engineering, nursing, data analysis)
Work placements and internships help young people make the transition into the labour market
Graduate unemployment is a waste of public investment in higher education
against: Many jobs that exist today will change or disappear, so narrow training quickly becomes outdated
Critical thinking and research skills learnt through 'pure' subjects are transferable to any job
Universities drive basic research that later produces practical benefits (e.g. the internet, vaccines)
A democratic society needs citizens educated in history, philosophy and science, not only workers

models.text:
It is often claimed that universities exist primarily to equip young people for the job market, and that studying a subject simply because it is interesting is a luxury. While I accept that employability is an important concern, I largely disagree with this view, because the most valuable thing a university can offer is a broad intellectual foundation that remains useful long after specific skills have become obsolete.

Admittedly, there are strong reasons why students and governments expect degrees to lead to work. Tuition fees in many countries are high, and graduates who leave with considerable debt understandably want a reasonable salary in return. Similarly, when the state subsidises higher education, taxpayers expect a return in the form of qualified doctors, engineers and teachers. Courses that include work placements, such as nursing or architecture, clearly serve both the individual and society.

However, defining a university purely as a training centre is short-sighted. The labour market is changing so rapidly that technical knowledge acquired at nineteen may be out of date by the time a graduate is thirty. What endures is the capacity to analyse evidence, construct an argument and learn independently, and these abilities are developed precisely through the kind of open-ended study that critics dismiss as impractical. A history graduate who has learnt to evaluate conflicting sources, for instance, is often well prepared for careers in law, journalism or policy analysis.

Furthermore, much of the research that eventually transforms economies begins as curiosity-driven inquiry. Work on the structure of DNA or on early computer networks had no obvious commercial application at the time, yet both have since created entire industries. If universities were judged only by short-term employment figures, this kind of fundamental research would be among the first casualties.

In conclusion, although preparing students for work is a legitimate aim, it should not be the main one. Universities serve individuals and society best when they cultivate flexible, critical minds, which in the long run also turn out to be the most employable.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): posición clara desde la introducción ('I largely disagree') y mantenida hasta la conclusión. Reconoce la postura contraria en un párrafo de concesión ('Admittedly...') y la rebate con dos argumentos completamente desarrollados (obsolescencia de las habilidades técnicas; investigación básica) con ejemplos concretos (graduado de historia, ADN). Coherence & Cohesion (8): cada párrafo tiene una idea central; los conectores son variados y naturales ('Admittedly', 'However', 'Furthermore'), y la referencia ('this kind of fundamental research', 'these abilities') une las frases sin forzar. Lexical Resource (8): léxico preciso y académico ('obsolete', 'short-sighted', 'curiosity-driven inquiry', 'first casualties') con colocaciones naturales. Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): mezcla de estructuras complejas (condicional 'If universities were judged...', relativas, pasivas, 'What endures is...') sin errores relevantes. Para llegar a 9: un argumento aún más matizado (p. ej., distinguir entre carreras profesionales y académicas) y un ejemplo todavía más específico en el párrafo de concesión.

models.text:
Nowadays many people believe that universities should mainly prepare students for their future jobs instead of teaching knowledge for its own sake. In my opinion, I partly agree with this, but I think that general knowledge is still more important.

On the one hand, it is true that most students go to university because they want a good job. University is very expensive in many countries, and students often finish their studies with a big loan. For this reason, they need practical skills that companies are looking for. For example, a computer science student who learns programming languages that are used in the industry will find a job more easily than one who only studies theory.

On the other hand, knowledge for its own sake has many benefits. Firstly, subjects like philosophy or literature teach students how to think critically and express their ideas clearly. These skills are useful in almost every job, even if they are not connected directly to a specific career. Secondly, technology changes very fast, so the skills that students learn today may not be needed in ten years. A person with a broad education can adapt more easily to these changes.

In addition, universities are also places for research. Many important discoveries started with research that did not have a practical purpose at first, but later it became very useful for society.

In conclusion, although preparing students for work is important, I believe universities should not forget their role of giving knowledge for its own sake, because it helps both the students and society in the long term.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): responde a la pregunta y da una postura, aunque 'I partly agree... but general knowledge is still more important' resulta algo ambigua (¿de acuerdo o en desacuerdo?). El ejemplo de informática está bien, pero el párrafo de investigación es breve y sin ejemplo concreto. Coherence & Cohesion (7): estructura clara y lógica, pero los conectores son algo previsibles ('On the one hand', 'Firstly', 'Secondly', 'In addition'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('critically', 'adapt', 'broad education'), aunque con expresiones generales ('a big loan', 'very useful', 'very fast'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): frases complejas mayoritariamente correctas; 'In my opinion, I partly agree' es redundante. Para subir a 8: formular la postura sin ambigüedad ('I largely disagree'), desarrollar cada idea con un ejemplo específico y sustituir intensificadores como 'very' por léxico más preciso ('rapidly', 'considerable debt').

models.text:
In today world, university education is very important for everyone. Some people think that university should prepare students for job, but other people think it should give knowledge. I will discuss about this topic in this essay.

Firstly, preparing for job is very important. Because the students spend a lot of money in university, they want to find a good job after they finish. If the university only teach theory, the students will not have the skills that the companies need. For example, in my country many graduates can not find a job and this is a big problem. My cousin studied biology for four years but now he work in a shop because he has no practical experience. So universities must teach more practical things like computer and business.

Secondly, knowledge is also important. Students who study subjects like history or art can learn many things about the world and this make them more cultured. Also, knowledge help people to think in a better way. Some jobs need general knowledge and not only practical skills, for example journalists or teachers must to know about many subjects.

Moreover, the world is changing very fast nowadays. Technology is developing and there are many new jobs. So students need to learn many different things in the university to be ready for the future. This is why both are important.

In conclusion, I think that preparing for job is the main purpose of university but knowledge is also important. Universities should teach both things so the students can have a good future and get a good job.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): trata ambos lados, pero la postura no queda clara hasta la conclusión, y allí contradice en parte el cuerpo ('This is why both are important' frente a 'preparing for job is the main purpose'). Las ideas son relevantes pero generales ('many things about the world', 'think in a better way') y el ejemplo de 'my country' no se desarrolla. Coherence & Cohesion (6): hay párrafos, pero el enlace es mecánico ('Firstly', 'Secondly', 'Moreover', 'So') y el tercer párrafo del cuerpo no tiene una idea central nítida. Lexical Resource (6): vocabulario limitado y repetitivo ('important' aparece muchas veces, 'good job', 'many things'); 'discuss about' es un error típico (discuss no lleva 'about'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores de concordancia ('the university only teach', 'this make', 'knowledge help'), artículos ('In today world', 'for job') y predominan las frases simples. Para subir a 7: anunciar la postura en la introducción y mantenerla, desarrollar un ejemplo concreto por párrafo, variar el vocabulario y revisar concordancia sujeto-verbo y artículos.

prompt:
Governments spend large amounts of money on space exploration. Some people believe that this money would be better spent on solving problems here on Earth.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: State clearly whether (and how far) you agree that the money should be spent on Earth's problems
Discuss the case for redirecting funds to problems on Earth
Discuss the value (or lack of value) of space exploration
Support each main idea with explanation and a relevant example
Keep the position consistent and restate it in the conclusion

for: Poverty, hunger and inadequate healthcare cause immediate suffering that money could relieve
Climate change requires urgent, very costly investment in clean energy and adaptation
Space programmes partly serve national prestige rather than real human needs
Private companies are now investing in space, so public money is less necessary
against: Space budgets are a tiny fraction of total public spending compared with health or defence
Satellites help solve Earth's problems: weather forecasting, disaster warnings, climate monitoring
Space research has produced spin-off technologies (water purification, medical imaging, GPS)
Exploration inspires young people to study science and engineering

models.text:
Space programmes are frequently criticised as an extravagant use of public funds at a time when millions of people lack clean water, adequate healthcare or secure housing. Although I understand the moral force of this argument, I disagree with it for the most part, since space exploration is not only relatively inexpensive but also contributes directly to solving many of the problems its critics highlight.

The case for redirecting funds is easy to appreciate. Money spent on a mission to Mars could, in theory, finance hospitals, schools or flood defences that would improve lives immediately. Moreover, some space projects appear to be driven as much by national prestige as by scientific need, which makes them an obvious target when budgets are tight.

Nevertheless, this argument rests on a misleading picture of the sums involved. In most countries that run space agencies, the budget amounts to well under one per cent of public expenditure, far less than is spent on defence or debt interest. Cancelling these programmes would therefore release relatively little money, while sacrificing a field of considerable long-term value.

More importantly, much of what is labelled 'space exploration' is in fact a tool for addressing earthly challenges. Satellite data underpins modern weather forecasting, allows governments to track deforestation and melting ice sheets, and provides early warnings of hurricanes and droughts that save thousands of lives. In addition, technologies first developed for spacecraft, from compact water filters to advances in medical imaging, have found widespread everyday use. Far from competing with efforts to improve life on Earth, space research often makes those efforts possible.

In conclusion, while governments must certainly prioritise urgent human needs, abandoning space exploration would be a false economy. A modest, well-managed investment in space yields knowledge and technologies that help us understand and protect our own planet.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): postura clara ('I disagree with it for the most part') y coherente. Concede la parte razonable del enunciado y luego desarrolla dos contraargumentos sólidos: el tamaño real del presupuesto y los beneficios directos para la Tierra (satélites, tecnología derivada), con ejemplos concretos. Coherence & Cohesion (8): progresión lógica impecable; 'Nevertheless' y 'More importantly' marcan la jerarquía de los argumentos; la frase final del cuarto párrafo resume la idea con naturalidad. Lexical Resource (8): léxico preciso y variado ('extravagant', 'moral force', 'national prestige', 'underpins', 'false economy'), con colocaciones idiomáticas. Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras variadas (participio 'Far from competing...', relativas, comparativas complejas) prácticamente sin errores. Para un 9: citar una cifra o caso aún más concreto y matizar qué tipo de misiones sí podrían recortarse, mostrando un razonamiento todavía más fino.

models.text:
Every year, governments in countries like the USA, China and India spend billions of dollars on space programmes. Some people think that this money should be used to solve problems on Earth, such as poverty and pollution. I partly agree with this idea, but I believe that space exploration should not be stopped completely.

There are several reasons why spending on Earth's problems seems more urgent. Many people in the world still live in poverty and do not have access to basic services like healthcare and education. In addition, climate change is causing serious problems, for example floods and droughts, and governments need a lot of money to deal with them. When people are suffering, it is difficult to justify sending rockets to other planets, especially in countries where many citizens cannot afford medicine.

However, space exploration also brings important benefits for people on Earth. Satellites are used to predict the weather and to monitor natural disasters, which helps to protect people's lives. Furthermore, many technologies that we use every day, like GPS on our phones, were developed through space research. Without this investment, our lives would be less convenient and less safe.

Another point is that space exploration encourages young people to study science and engineering. When children see astronauts or new discoveries about other planets, they become interested in science, and this can help the country's economy in the future.

In conclusion, although problems on Earth are very important and should be a priority, I think governments should continue to invest some money in space exploration because it gives many benefits to humanity.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): responde con una postura comprensible y relevante, aunque 'I partly agree' acaba defendiendo sobre todo la exploración espacial, por lo que la posición podría ser más precisa. Las ideas son pertinentes, pero el párrafo sobre inspirar a los jóvenes queda poco desarrollado. Coherence & Cohesion (7): buena organización y progresión; conectores correctos pero algo convencionales ('In addition', 'However', 'Furthermore', 'Another point is'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('justify', 'monitor natural disasters'), con algunas expresiones vagas ('a lot of money', 'many benefits', 'very important'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buena variedad (relativas, condicional 'Without this investment...'), errores muy escasos. Para subir a 8: formular la postura exacta ('I largely disagree'), añadir un argumento clave (el presupuesto espacial es pequeño en proporción) y usar léxico más preciso en vez de 'a lot of' o 'many benefits'.

models.text:
Nowadays, space exploration is a very popular topic and many countries spend a lot of money on it. However, some people believe that this money should be spend on the problems on Earth. In my opinion, I agree with this statement for some reasons.

First of all, there are a lot of problems in the world today. For example, many people are poor and they don't have food or a house. Also there are many diseases and the hospitals need more money for help the patients. If the governments use the money of space for these problems, the life of many people will be better. I think this is more important than to go to the moon or Mars. Helping people who are suffering now must be the first priority of every government.

Second, the environment is a big problem. The pollution is increasing every year and the climate is changing. The governments must to spend money to protect the nature, for example to build more solar energy. Space exploration don't help with this problem.

On the other hand, space exploration have some advantages. Scientists can discover new things about the universe and some technology like satellites is useful for people. But I think these advantages are not enough compare with the problems we have.

To conclude, I agree that the money of space exploration should be use to solve the problems on Earth like poverty and environment, because these problems are more urgent and they affect to millions of people every day.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): postura clara ('I agree') y mantenida, con ideas relevantes, pero muy generales y poco desarrolladas ('many people are poor', 'the environment is a big problem'). Además, afirma que la exploración espacial 'don't help' con el medio ambiente, lo cual es discutible (satélites climáticos) y el texto no lo matiza. Coherence & Cohesion (6): estructura reconocible, pero enlaces mecánicos ('First of all', 'Second', 'Also', 'But') y uso repetido de 'the governments'. Lexical Resource (6): vocabulario básico y repetitivo ('a lot of', 'problems' aparece muchas veces); colocaciones poco naturales ('the money of space', 'protect the nature'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores frecuentes que no impiden la comprensión: 'should be spend/use', 'must to spend', 'for help the patients', 'space exploration don't/have', 'compare with', 'affect to'. Para subir a 7: desarrollar cada idea con un ejemplo concreto y su consecuencia, reconocer y rebatir mejor el argumento contrario, y revisar formas verbales tras modales y la concordancia.

prompt:
The most effective way to reduce crime is to give offenders longer prison sentences.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: State clearly how far you agree that longer sentences are the MOST effective way
Evaluate the effect of longer prison sentences on crime
Consider at least one alternative way of reducing crime (the prompt says 'most effective')
Support ideas with explanation and examples
Keep the position consistent and restate it in the conclusion

for: Dangerous offenders in prison cannot commit further crimes against the public
Severe punishment may deter potential criminals
Victims and society may feel that justice has been done
Long sentences send a clear message about which crimes society considers serious
against: Research suggests the certainty of being caught deters more than the length of the sentence
Prisons can act as 'schools of crime', and many released prisoners reoffend
Prisons are expensive; money could fund education, policing and rehabilitation
Tackling root causes (poverty, addiction, lack of education) prevents crime before it happens

models.text:
When crime rates rise, politicians often respond by promising tougher sentences, and many voters assume that keeping offenders behind bars for longer is the surest way to make streets safer. In my view, however, this belief is largely mistaken: longer prison terms play a limited role, and other measures are considerably more effective in reducing crime.

It would be unrealistic to deny that imprisonment has some value. A violent offender who is in prison is, quite simply, unable to harm the public, and for the most serious crimes lengthy sentences are both a necessary protection and an appropriate expression of society's condemnation.

The problem is that the deterrent effect of long sentences appears to be weak. Most crimes are committed impulsively, often under the influence of alcohol or drugs, by people who do not expect to be caught at all. For such individuals, the difference between a three-year and a six-year sentence is largely irrelevant. Criminologists have consistently found that the likelihood of being arrested deters far more effectively than the severity of the punishment, which suggests that investment in policing would achieve more than investment in prison cells.

Moreover, prison frequently makes offenders more, not less, dangerous. Inmates mix with experienced criminals, lose contact with their families and find it extremely difficult to obtain work on release, so it is hardly surprising that a large proportion reoffend within a few years. By contrast, countries such as Norway, which emphasise education and vocational training inside prison, report some of the lowest reoffending rates in the world.

In conclusion, while long sentences remain appropriate for the most dangerous criminals, they are far from the most effective way of reducing crime. A combination of visible policing, rehabilitation and efforts to tackle the causes of offending, such as addiction and unemployment, offers a far better return for society.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): entiende el matiz clave del enunciado ('the MOST effective way') y responde con precisión: las condenas largas tienen un papel limitado, pero otras medidas son más eficaces. Concede lo razonable (proteger al público) y desarrolla dos argumentos con ejemplos (delitos impulsivos; Noruega). Coherence & Cohesion (8): párrafos con una función clara (concesión, disuasión, reincidencia); conectores naturales ('The problem is that', 'Moreover', 'By contrast'). Lexical Resource (8): léxico temático preciso ('deterrent effect', 'reoffend', 'vocational training', 'condemnation', 'behind bars') y estilo natural ('quite simply', 'hardly surprising'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): gran variedad (relativas no especificativas, comparativas, 'more, not less, dangerous'), sin errores significativos. Para un 9: aún más precisión en algún dato y un cierre que integre las soluciones con algo más de profundidad.

models.text:
Some people believe that giving criminals longer prison sentences is the best way to reduce crime. Although I agree that prison is necessary for serious crimes, I do not think it is the most effective solution.

On the one hand, long prison sentences have some advantages. First, when dangerous criminals are in prison, they cannot hurt other people, so society is safer. Second, people may think twice before committing a crime if they know the punishment is very severe. For example, in some countries the punishment for drug smuggling is extremely strict, and this may stop some people from doing it. Victims of crime may also feel that justice has been done.

On the other hand, there are better ways to reduce crime. Many prisoners commit crimes again after they are released, because in prison they meet other criminals and they do not learn any useful skills. If prisons offered education and job training, prisoners would have more chances to find a job and live a normal life after prison. This would reduce crime more than simply keeping them in prison for longer.

In addition, it is important to deal with the causes of crime. Many crimes are connected to poverty, drugs or lack of education. If governments invest in schools, youth centres and programmes for drug addicts, fewer people will become criminals in the first place.

In conclusion, although longer sentences can protect society from dangerous people, I believe that education, rehabilitation and solving social problems are more effective ways to reduce crime in the long term.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): postura clara y coherente; analiza ventajas de las condenas largas y propone alternativas. Sin embargo, el argumento de la disuasión se presenta sin cuestionarlo, lo que debilita un poco la posición, y el último párrafo del cuerpo es general (sin ejemplo concreto). Coherence & Cohesion (7): organización clara con 'On the one hand / On the other hand', aunque los conectores son algo esquemáticos ('First', 'Second', 'In addition'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado y temático ('rehabilitation', 'drug smuggling', 'think twice', 'in the first place'), con alguna repetición ('crime' muchas veces). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buen uso de condicionales de segundo y primer tipo; errores mínimos. Para subir a 8: rebatir explícitamente la idea de la disuasión (la certeza de ser detenido pesa más que la duración), dar ejemplos más específicos y variar el léxico con sinónimos ('offenders', 'inmates', 'reoffending').

models.text:
Crime is a serious problem in many countries in the world. Some people think that the best solution is to give criminals longer time in prison. I partly agree with this opinion.

Firstly, longer prison sentences can make the people more safe. When a criminal is in the prison for many years, he can not do more crimes. For example, if a person kill someone, he should stay in prison for very long time because he is dangerous for the society. The families of the victims also want a strong punishment. Also, other people will be afraid to do crimes because they don't want to go to prison.

However, prison is not always the best solution. In the prison the criminals meet another criminals and they learn more bad things. When they go out, they do crimes again. Also prison is very expensive for the government and the tax payers have to pay for it.

In my opinion, the government should also do other things. For example, they can give more education to young people and create more jobs. Many people do crimes because they are poor and they don't have job. If they have a good job they will not need to steal. The police also should be more in the streets.

In conclusion, longer prison sentences is a good way to reduce crime for dangerous criminals, but the government also need to give education and jobs to the people. Both ways are necessary to reduce crime in the society.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): responde a la pregunta y propone alternativas, pero 'I partly agree' no queda bien definido y las ideas se enumeran más que se desarrollan (p. ej., la policía en la calle aparece en una sola frase al final). No aborda con claridad si las condenas largas son 'the most effective way'. Coherence & Cohesion (6): estructura en párrafos correcta, pero conectores repetitivos ('Also' tres veces, 'Firstly', 'However') y algunas ideas sin relación clara dentro del párrafo. Lexical Resource (6): léxico limitado y repetitivo ('do crimes' en lugar de 'commit crimes', 'bad things', 'very long time'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores frecuentes: 'more safe' (safer), 'if a person kill', 'another criminals', 'longer prison sentences is', 'the government also need', 'for very long time'. Para subir a 7: definir la postura con precisión, desarrollar cada alternativa con un ejemplo y su efecto, usar colocaciones correctas ('commit a crime', 'reoffend') y revisar concordancia y artículos.

prompt:
Some people believe that working from home benefits both employees and employers. Others argue that it has a negative effect on productivity and teamwork.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: Discuss the view that working from home benefits employees and employers
Discuss the view that it harms productivity and teamwork
Give your own opinion clearly (in the introduction and/or conclusion, and consistently)
Support both views with explanation and examples
Give the two views roughly equal attention

for: No commuting saves time, money and stress, and reduces traffic and emissions
Fewer interruptions allow deeper concentration on individual tasks
Employers save on office space and can recruit talent from anywhere
Flexibility helps parents and carers stay in the workforce
against: Spontaneous conversations and creative exchanges happen less online
New and junior staff learn less without observing experienced colleagues
Some employees struggle with distractions or isolation at home
Boundaries between work and private life become blurred, leading to burnout

models.text:
Since the pandemic, working from home has shifted from a rare privilege to a routine arrangement for millions of office workers. Supporters regard it as a gain for everyone involved, whereas critics claim that it undermines productivity and collaboration. Having considered both perspectives, I believe that a hybrid model, combining home and office work, captures most of the benefits while limiting the drawbacks.

Those who favour remote work point first to the time and money it saves. An employee who no longer spends ninety minutes a day commuting can devote that time to rest, family or the work itself, and is often less stressed as a result. Many people also find that, away from the noise of an open-plan office, they can concentrate on demanding tasks for longer periods. Employers benefit too: they can reduce expensive office space and recruit skilled staff who live far from the company's headquarters.

On the other hand, sceptics argue that something important is lost when colleagues rarely meet. Much innovation stems from informal conversations that are difficult to reproduce on a video call, and team spirit can weaken when communication is reduced to scheduled meetings and messages. Junior employees are particularly disadvantaged, since they learn a great deal simply by observing how experienced colleagues handle clients or solve problems. In addition, some workers find it hard to separate their professional and private lives at home, which may eventually lead to exhaustion.

In my view, both arguments are valid, which is precisely why an all-or-nothing approach is unwise. Allowing staff to work from home for focused individual tasks, while bringing teams together on fixed days for planning, training and creative work, enables organisations to keep the flexibility employees value without sacrificing cohesion.

In conclusion, working from home offers genuine advantages, but it cannot fully replace the social dimension of the workplace. A carefully designed hybrid arrangement is, I believe, the most sensible solution for both employees and employers.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): discute ambos puntos de vista con desarrollo equilibrado y da una opinión clara y coherente (modelo híbrido) en la introducción, un párrafo propio y la conclusión. Cubre empleados y empleadores, como pide el enunciado. Coherence & Cohesion (8): estructura ideal para discussion (vista A, vista B, opinión); los conectores ('On the other hand', 'In addition', 'which is precisely why') fluyen con naturalidad. Lexical Resource (8): vocabulario preciso y natural ('routine arrangement', 'open-plan office', 'stems from', 'all-or-nothing approach', 'cohesion'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras complejas variadas (relativas, gerundios, participios 'Having considered...') sin errores relevantes. Para un 9: ejemplos aún más específicos (un sector o empresa concreta) y algún matiz adicional, p. ej., que el modelo ideal depende del tipo de trabajo.

models.text:
Working from home has become very common in recent years, especially after the Covid-19 pandemic. Some people think that it is good for both workers and companies, while others believe that it reduces productivity and makes teamwork more difficult. This essay will discuss both views before giving my own opinion.

On the one hand, there are clear benefits of working from home. Employees do not have to travel to the office every day, so they save time and money. For instance, someone who lives in a big city like London may spend more than two hours a day on public transport. Without this, they have more energy for their work and more free time for their families. Companies can also save money because they need smaller offices.

On the other hand, some people argue that working from home has negative effects. When people work alone, it is more difficult to share ideas and solve problems together. Communication through emails and video calls is often slower and less effective than face-to-face meetings. Moreover, some employees are easily distracted at home, for example by children or housework, and this can reduce their productivity.

In my opinion, working from home is beneficial, but it should not replace the office completely. I think the best solution is to work from home for two or three days a week and go to the office on the other days. This way, employees can enjoy flexibility and still keep good relationships with their colleagues.

In conclusion, although working from home has some disadvantages, I believe that a combination of home and office work is the best option for most people.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): discute ambos puntos de vista y da una opinión clara, con un ejemplo concreto (Londres). La opinión aparece de forma algo tardía (la introducción sólo anuncia 'This essay will discuss...'), y el argumento sobre los empleadores es breve. Coherence & Cohesion (7): estructura clara; conectores correctos pero previsibles ('On the one hand', 'On the other hand', 'Moreover', 'This way'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('flexibility', 'easily distracted', 'face-to-face'), aunque algo general ('good for', 'clear benefits'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buen control, frases complejas correctas y apenas errores. Para subir a 8: avanzar la opinión en la introducción, desarrollar más el punto de vista del empleador (reclutar talento, coste de oficinas) y emplear léxico más preciso y menos genérico.

models.text:
Nowadays a lot of people are working from home because of the technology. Some people say that this is good for the workers and the companies, but other people think that it is bad for the productivity and the teamwork. In this essay I will discuss both opinions.

In one hand, working from home has many advantages. The workers don't need to go to the office, so they can save money of transport and they have more time. Also they can wear comfortable clothes and work in a relax environment. This make them more happy and when people are happy they work better. The companies also can save money because they don't need big offices.

In the other hand, working from home have some disadvantages. Some people can not concentrate at home because there are many distractions like the TV or the family. Also it is difficult to work in team when everybody is in different place. The boss can not control if the workers are working or not. For this reasons, some companies want that the workers come back to the office. Young workers also can not learn from the experienced colleagues if they never see them.

In my opinion, I think working from home is a good idea but not for everybody. Some people work better at home and other people work better in the office. It depends of the person and the type of job.

In conclusion, working from home has advantages and disadvantages. The companies should let the workers to choose where they want to work.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): aborda ambos puntos de vista y da una opinión ('depends on the person'), pero las ideas son superficiales y sin ejemplos concretos; la opinión de la conclusión (que elijan los trabajadores) aparece de repente sin desarrollo. Coherence & Cohesion (6): estructura correcta, pero conectores mecánicos y con errores ('In one hand' y 'In the other hand' deben ser 'On'); 'Also' se repite. Lexical Resource (6): vocabulario básico ('good', 'bad', 'many advantages'); errores de forma ('a relax environment' → relaxed, 'money of transport' → transport costs). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores frecuentes: 'This make them more happy', 'working from home have', 'For this reasons', 'want that the workers come' (want the workers to come), 'let the workers to choose', 'depends of'. Para subir a 7: incluir un ejemplo concreto por punto de vista, desarrollar la opinión con un razonamiento y revisar estructuras verbales típicas de hispanohablantes (want + object + to, let + infinitivo sin to, depend on).

prompt:
Some people believe that growing cities should build upwards, with more high-rise buildings. Others think that cities should instead expand outwards into the surrounding countryside.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: Discuss the view that cities should build upwards (high-rise development)
Discuss the view that cities should expand outwards
Give your own opinion and keep it consistent
Support both views with reasons and examples
Conclude by summarising both views and your position

for: High-rise development protects farmland, forests and green belts around cities
Dense cities make public transport, cycling and walking practical, reducing car use
Shorter distances to jobs and services save time and energy
Infrastructure (water, power, transport) is cheaper per person in compact cities
against: Suburban housing offers more space, gardens and quieter surroundings, especially for families
Tall buildings can feel crowded and isolating, and may be expensive to build and maintain
Land on the edge of cities is cheaper, which can make housing more affordable
High-rise areas can block light and change the character of historic city centres

models.text:
As urban populations continue to grow, planners face a fundamental choice: should cities accommodate new residents by building taller, or by spreading further into the countryside? Both approaches have committed supporters, but I would argue that carefully planned vertical growth is generally the more sustainable option.

Advocates of outward expansion emphasise quality of life. Suburban homes typically offer more space, private gardens and quieter streets, which many families regard as essential for raising children. Land on the urban fringe is also usually cheaper than in the centre, so new housing developments there can be more affordable for first-time buyers. Furthermore, some residents simply dislike high-rise living, associating it with overcrowding, a lack of community and, in poorly managed estates, social problems.

Those who favour building upwards, by contrast, focus on the environmental and economic costs of sprawl. Every new suburb consumes farmland or natural habitat that can never easily be recovered, and residents of low-density areas depend heavily on private cars because public transport is rarely viable when homes are widely scattered. Compact cities, on the other hand, allow shops, schools and workplaces to be within walking or cycling distance, and they make metro and bus networks efficient. Singapore and Hong Kong, for example, house millions of people on limited land while maintaining excellent public transport.

In my opinion, the arguments for density are more persuasive, although the concerns about liveability deserve to be taken seriously. High-rise development succeeds when it is combined with parks, good design and local services, rather than consisting of isolated tower blocks. Medium-rise neighbourhoods of six to ten storeys, common in cities such as Barcelona, show that density need not mean an inhuman scale.

In conclusion, although suburban expansion offers space and affordability, it does so at a high environmental cost. Cities should therefore grow mainly upwards, provided that vertical development is designed around the needs of the people who live there.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): discute ambos puntos de vista con equilibrio y profundidad, y da una opinión clara ('carefully planned vertical growth') que mantiene y matiza (la densidad debe ir acompañada de parques, diseño y servicios). Ejemplos específicos y pertinentes (Singapur, Hong Kong, Barcelona). Coherence & Cohesion (8): progresión muy clara; 'by contrast', 'on the other hand', 'therefore' y la referencia ('the concerns about liveability') guían al lector sin artificio. Lexical Resource (8): léxico temático preciso ('urban fringe', 'sprawl', 'low-density', 'liveability', 'storeys', 'first-time buyers') y colocaciones naturales. Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): variedad de estructuras (relativas, condicionales con 'provided that', pasivas) con precisión casi total. Para un 9: algo más de análisis sobre los costes de construir en altura (mantenimiento, energía) para que la opinión sea aún más matizada.

models.text:
Many cities around the world are growing quickly, and governments have to decide how to provide enough housing. Some people think the answer is to build more tall buildings, while others believe that cities should spread into the countryside. In this essay, I will discuss both opinions and explain why I prefer building upwards.

On the one hand, expanding cities outwards has some benefits. Houses in the suburbs are usually bigger and cheaper than flats in the city centre, and they often have gardens. This is attractive for families with children who want more space and a quieter environment. In addition, many people do not like living in very tall buildings because they feel crowded and they do not know their neighbours.

On the other hand, building upwards has important advantages. Firstly, it protects the countryside, because cities do not need to use farmland or forests for new houses. Secondly, when people live close together, public transport becomes more efficient. For example, in cities like Tokyo, most people use the train every day because stations are near their homes. In contrast, people who live in distant suburbs usually need a car, which causes traffic jams and pollution.

In my opinion, building upwards is the better solution, especially for big cities with limited space. However, the government should make sure that high-rise areas also have parks and public spaces, so that residents can enjoy a good quality of life.

In conclusion, both options have advantages, but I believe that building upwards is more sustainable for the future of our cities.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): trata ambas posturas y da una opinión clara y mantenida, con un buen ejemplo (Tokio). El desarrollo es correcto, aunque algo menos profundo: por ejemplo, no explica por qué el transporte público funciona mejor con densidad más allá de 'stations are near'. Coherence & Cohesion (7): organización clara; conectores adecuados pero algo previsibles ('On the one hand', 'Firstly', 'Secondly', 'In contrast'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('suburbs', 'farmland', 'high-rise areas', 'sustainable'), con algunas expresiones generales ('important advantages', 'good quality of life'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): estructuras complejas correctas (relativas, 'so that'), errores casi inexistentes. Para subir a 8: desarrollar más el razonamiento (coste de infraestructuras, pérdida irreversible de suelo), usar léxico más preciso ('urban sprawl', 'density') y conectores más integrados en el texto.

models.text:
Nowadays many cities are getting bigger and bigger because more people move to them. Some people think that the cities should build tall buildings, but other people think that it is better to build in the countryside around the city. Both opinions have good and bad points.

Firstly, building tall buildings is good because it use less land. In big cities there is not much space, so the only way is to build up. Also, people can live near to their work and they don't need to travel a lot. For example in New York there are many skyscrapers and many people live and work in the center.

Secondly, other people prefer to live outside the city. They think the houses in the countryside are more big and more cheap. Also the air is more clean and there is less noise. Families with children like to have a garden where the children can play. But the problem is that they need a car to go to the city and this produce a lot of traffic.

In my opinion, I think both ways are good but it depends of the city. If the city is very big and crowded, it is better to build tall buildings. If the city is small and there is a lot of land, it can grow to the countryside. The government must to think about what is better for each city.

In conclusion, building upwards and outwards both have advantages and disadvantages, and the government should choose the best way for the people.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): discute las dos posturas y da una opinión ('depends on the city'), lo cual es válido, pero las ideas son generales y poco desarrolladas, y la conclusión no aporta una posición nítida. El ejemplo de Nueva York se menciona sin explicar su relevancia. Coherence & Cohesion (6): 'Firstly' y 'Secondly' se usan para presentar dos puntos de vista distintos, lo cual es mecánico e impreciso; 'Also' se repite. Lexical Resource (6): vocabulario básico ('good and bad points', 'build up', 'a lot of'); la expresión 'getting bigger and bigger' es informal para un ensayo. Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores de comparativos ('more big', 'more cheap', 'more clean'), concordancia ('it use', 'this produce'), 'depends of', 'must to think', 'near to their work'. Para subir a 7: presentar cada punto de vista con su propio razonamiento y ejemplo, desarrollar la opinión con criterios claros y dominar comparativos y formas verbales básicas.
